title: Region priority controller — p50/p95 delta and path integrity index
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: implement a region-priority controller that synthesizes latency quantiles (p50, p95) and a network path integrity index to decide preferred POPs for routing and to trigger tier-aware fallback model variants. Motivation: current routing relies on single percentile signals and separate link health gates. This ticket designs and implements a unified score that captures latency dispersion and network quality, enabling more robust short-circuit decisions and safer soft-fallbacks to model variants when needed.

Core idea: compute a quantile_gap = (p95 - p50) / max(p50, 1ms) for each region over a rolling 60s window; compute path_loss_score from packet-loss EWMA and jitter percentiles; combine into path_integrity_index = sigmoid( - (w_q*quantile_gap + w_l*path_loss_score + w_h*hop_penalty) ) to yield a 0..1 integrity score (higher is healthier). Final region_priority_score = alpha*latency_p50_rank + beta*(1 - quantile_gap_norm) + gamma*path_integrity_index + tier_adjustment.

Tier behavior: for Dedicated and Enterprise tiers we favor region affinity and only perform hard-failover on integrity<0.2. For Hosted tier we allow more aggressive soft-fallbacks when integrity<0.5 with throttled traffic shifting and model-variant fallback chains (e.g., full FP16 -> q4_0 -> q4_1 quantized variant).

Implementation notes: aggregation will live in the telemetry aggregator (metric-merge service). Scoring runs in the region-decider service with a feature flag. We will expose tuning weights via config and surface key metrics on a new Grafana panel.

Expected outcomes: fewer noisy cross-region failovers, lower p95 for tail-sensitive customers, controlled increase in fallback to quantized variants with rollup metrics to detect quality regressions.
comments: 2025-01-11 - Maya: initial writeup and math for quantile_gap and path_integrity_index. Posted design doc to Confluence.
2025-01-14 - Architecture review with infra and runtime teams. Agreed scoring should run in region-decider, not at edge proxies due to data enrichment needs. Liam to prototype scoring module.

2025-01-22 - Prototype complete: scoring module computes quantile_gap and path_loss_score using 60s sliding windows. Observed sensitivity to p50 noise at low qps; added min-sample threshold (n>=50) and fallback to EWMA when under threshold.
2025-01-29 - UX/PM feedback: require visibility in Console for per-customer tier rules and ability to pin region. Added console hooks in plan.
2025-02-05 - Engineering: integrated path_loss metrics (packet_loss_percentile, retransmit_rate) from telemetry pipeline. Created Grafana dashboard panel routing.v2.region_score (link in links).

2025-02-12 - QA: ran canary traffic (10k reqs/min) against canary region and simulated packet loss 1-5%. Observed 12% of requests moved to fallback q4_0 variant for Hosted tier. PM accepted as within threshold but flagged need for quality monitoring alert. Added acceptance criterion to require eval-rate < 20% fallback and no output-quality regressions above 0.5 BLEU drop on synthetic prompts.
2025-02-18 - Security review: no data retention changes. Security ok with config access control. Moving to in-progress implementation of rollout automation.
decision: Adopt a composite region_priority_score that combines p50, normalized p95-p50 gap (quantile_gap), and a path_integrity_index derived from packet-loss and jitter. Tier-specific thresholds govern when to soft-fallback to lower-cost or quantized model variants. Run scoring centrally in region-decider with config flags and Console visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring module returns stable region_priority_score for all POPs with sample size >= 50
No more than 20% of Hosted traffic is routed to fallback model variants during a 1-hour test under induced packet loss (1-5%)
p95 latency for enterprise SLO customers does not regress >5% after rollout in five production minutes
Grafana panel routing.v2.region_score shows per-region components (p50, p95, quantile_gap, path_integrity_index)
Rollout automation supports gradual traffic shift with hysteresis and can be disabled via feature flag
metrics: target_p95_reduction: 10% for tier=hosted in degraded scenarios
fallback_rate_target: <20% Hosted during degraded link tests
next_steps: Finalize config schema and feature flag (Liam)
Merge PR for scoring module and run canary in eu-west (engineering)
Add Console UI toggle and per-customer override (product)
Run end-to-end quality evals on fallback variants with Solutions sample set
tradeoffs: Stronger sensitivity to quantile_gap reduces noisy cross-region shifts but may increase fallback to quantized variants, potentially impacting output quality
Centralized scoring simplifies enforcement but adds dependency on metric pipeline latency; mitigated by local cache and EWMA fallback
Tiered policies add complexity to routing logic and Console, but provide necessary predictability for Dedicated customers
risk_mitigation: Hysteresis windows (60s entry, 180s exit) to prevent flip-flop
Min-sample thresholds and EWMA fallback to avoid reacting to sparse traffic noise
Controlled rollout with traffic caps and quick kill switch via feature flag
Quality monitoring connected to Optimize pipeline to roll back variant mapping on regressions
